chapter_note: This chapter is overwhelmingly core cosmological teaching: First Man’s descent and the stripping of the storehouses, followed by correspondential analogies (marsh; human body/head and limbs; corpse). The only clear later material is the formulaic dialogue-attribution opening in ¶1, which functions as hagiographic frame around an otherwise core paragraph. Despite the chapter-level ‘fatigue’ signal, no explicit institutional/pastoral or NT overlay appears in the surviving paragraphs.

paragraphs.core_text: At the time when the First Man was sent to the war in the first garment of [living fire], which he gave to the first nature that exists [...] in that single garment. [...] he hunted Matter, the thought of Death, [...] and all its other powers.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the dialogue/frame attribution: “Once again the enlightener speaks:” (hagiographic compilation frame).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opening is a classic Kephalaia frame formula (“Once again…” + speaker attribution), but the remainder is impersonal cosmological narration about First Man’s garment of living fire and the hunting/snaring of Matter and Death-powers—internal to the Manichaean cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: When the First Man came up from the abyss, [...] the Living Spirit brought the rulers whom he had hunted [...] element, that [...] of [the land of] Darkness, that he might construct from them this universe and fashion everything appropriate for the Greatness. From that time on, the place of the storehouses of the elements [...] he destroyed and laid waste the [...] all that were in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic cosmological process-description (ascent from abyss; Living Spirit’s construction of the universe from captured rulers; devastation of storehouses). No citation, exhortation, or institutional mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: Just like a marsh, of which the fish and birds are snared in a net, and only the waters are left behind and the reeds and the plants that grow in it, this is also the case with the storehouses of Death. The [First] Man snared their counsels and [their k]in that were [in them], and the storehouses were left behind in their [dwelli]ng place.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Correspondential natural analogy (marsh/netted fish and birds) used to describe a cosmic condition (barren storehouses). The mapping stays cosmos↔nature without pointing to contemporary institutions.

paragraphs.core_text: So then, the case of the land of Darkness is like this, as is that of the storehouses that were in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief summative closure in the same impersonal expository voice; still purely cosmological.

paragraphs.core_text: Just as the body of man has many limbs in it, [the land of Darkness] has [storehouses from] its beginning [...] all [the limbs] that hang from the great head of the [body]. A single root is the root of them all, because they all hang from the great head that is on top of the body. Should a limb be cut from the tip of [the]se small [h]eads, the great head that is on top of them [al]l stays in its place the way that it is [...] you find this person alive. Al[l] these sm[all h]eads are firmly set in it [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extended body-cosmos correspondence (storehouses as limbs depending on a great head/root). No pastoral ‘you should…’ application; the brief ‘you find’ functions as explanatory rhetoric within the analogy, not audience exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: Wh[en] they will cut from them [...] all of them, these little [heads] shall [...] the corpses, because they might see [...] be firmly set [...] in the body, which they joined wi[th it ...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Lacunal continuation of the head/limbs analogy, still within the same correspondential explanatory register (corpse/body imagery) and without later institutional or citation markers.

paragraphs.core_text: In exactly this way, it is also the case that the storehouses of Darkness are the same, the things from which the [Darkness gushed] forth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concluding applicative phrase (“In exactly this way…”) refers back to the internal analogy and restates the cosmological claim; it does not pivot to church/institutional application, so it remains core.
